key_insight: Intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites is controlled by the energy position of halide-p bands relative to the valence-band maximum, rather than atomic spin–orbit strength.
engineering_relevance: Hole-gated CsPbI3 could provide a tunable spin-current source for perovskite spin–orbit torque devices, rather than a demonstrated solar-cell performance improvement.
method: First-principles calculations for CsPbBr3, CsPbI3, CsSnBr3 and CsSnI3.
Analysis of spin Berry curvature from spin–orbit-split halide-p bands.
Evaluation of intrinsic spin Hall conductivity versus Fermi level and hole density.
evidence_signal: Calculations locate the key halide-p bands 1.1–2.6 eV below the valence-band maximum and predict that CsPbI3 reaches p-GaAs-like spin Hall conductivity at hole densities accessible by electric double-layer gating.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions; experimentally achieving the required hole density while maintaining material stability and effective spin-current extraction remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
